title: Chart of accounts
summary: How classifications, types, and accounts fit together.

paragraphs.text: Your chart is three layers deep, and each layer has a job. Classifications (Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue, Expense) are fixed by the system—they tell reports how to treat balances. Account types sit in the middle; you might have “Bank” or “Credit card” under Asset. Accounts are the names you pick when you post—Checking, Groceries, and so on.

Getting the structure right early makes reports and budget planning much less confusing later. You do not need dozens of types on day one; start with what you actually use and add more when a real account does not fit anywhere.
